1.title: Precise Sugar and Alcohol Thresholds
1.html:
Level 1 already introduced the basic rules for VT and SGN; here we go deeper into the official precise figures — taking the current thresholds as an example (the VT values have been raised from the old regime of the 2007 harvest year, which was Gewurztraminer / Pinot Gris 257 g/L and Riesling / Muscat 235 g/L; SGN is unchanged):

Sugar (g/L)Minimum alcoholSugar (g/L)Minimum alcohol
Gewurztraminer27016.0°30618.2°
Pinot Gris27016.0°30618.2°

2.title: Seven Mandatory Production Conditions
2.html:
1. Must be hand harvested
  2. Must come from a single variety and be declared and sold under that variety's name
  3. Must reach the minimum natural sugar specified in the table
  4. No chaptalisation of any kind (enrichissement)
  5. Must reach the minimum total alcohol corresponding to the sugar level
  6. Prior declaration to the local INAO office is required before harvest
  7. Must pass dual approval by analysis and sensory tasting before the special VT / SGN labelling may be used
3.title: Climate Foundation: A Gift of the Semi-Continental Climate
3.html: Alsace's semi-continental climate has extremely low rainfall, together with exceptionally generous autumn sunshine — a combination that in good vintages especially favours the development of "passerillage" (drying and concentration on the vine) and noble rot (pourriture noble), making possible late-harvest and noble-rot selection long after the normal harvest period, and letting the four varieties Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Muscat show their richest and fullest side once fully ripe.
4.question: What is one of the strictest production conditions for VT and SGN noble-rot sweet wines?
4.options.0: Moderate chaptalisation is allowed to reach the target sweetness
4.options.1: Any form of chaptalisation (enrichissement) is forbidden, and the sugar must come entirely from the grapes' own natural concentration
4.options.2: Mechanical harvesting may be used to improve efficiency
4.options.3: No declaration to any official body is needed
4.explanation: The core spirit of VT and SGN is "purely natural concentration" — the regulations expressly forbid any form of chaptalisation (enrichissement). All the sweetness must be achieved through the natural action of late harvest (passerillage, drying and concentration) or noble rot (pourriture noble), which is why Alsace's dry, low-rainfall, sun-rich autumn climate is so crucial.
5.message: The strict VT and SGN rules complete!
